decisions.reason: As a standard bread product closely tied to the firm's existing baking know-how, it fits the core business and is relatively easy to refine from routine market feedback, so management would be inclined to retain it.

A sweet pastry is still well within the firm's established product knowledge, though pastries can be more assortment-sensitive than staple breads, so it is likely kept but with somewhat higher review risk.

A crusty farmhouse bread strongly builds on the firm's accumulated bread-making capabilities and can be improved through existing recipes, production experience, and customer response, making continuation likely.
The gold award signals strong early validation for this poppy seed Christmas stollen, and because seasonal stollen production relies on familiar bakery competences, the firm would likely continue it.

The premium Christmas stollen combines high relatedness to the firm's core knowledge with external quality recognition, which under an absorptive-capacity view makes it a strong candidate to keep and further exploit commercially.
